newsitem.title: UK: Cable & Wireless shares up on German alliance.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless shares up on German alliance.

text.p: Shares in Cable & Wireless rose in pre-market trade Wednesday after a German utility company said it had scrapped plans to form an alliance with British Telecom and was now planning an alliance with BT's main rival instead.
Shares in Cable and Wireless were indicated 4-1/2p higher at 438-1/2p by 0715 GMT and British Telecom shares fell 5p to 351p.

German utility company RWE AG said earlier today it was pulling out of its telecoms venture with Viag AG and British Telecom and is now in the final stages of talks with Veba AG and Cable & Wireless instead.
The announcement came as Germany prepares to award a licence next year to the country's fourth mobile phone network.
Viag said its partnership with British Telecom will continue without the third partner.

"The alliance is a definite positive for Cable & Wireless," Hepburn said. "Cable will incur much lower start-up losses as RWE moves in to take its share." said Michael Hepburn, analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
Analysts speculated that British Telecom may now aim for a closer relationship with Thyssen, another German mobile phone network bidder.
"The break-up is bad news for British Telecom, it translates to increased capital expenditures and further earnings dilution if RWE is missing from the equation," Hepburn said.
